full_text:
13,779 individuals reached in 2026 by Child Protection, Gender Based Violence (GBV) Prevention and Response, and Mental Health & Psychosocial Support (MHPSS)

168 older persons and persons with disabilities reached

73% Female

27% Male

58% Children

Case management

UNHCR’s integrated case management approach in Syria provides individualized and confidential support to children at risk, survivors of gender-based violence, and individuals experiencing mental health and psychosocial distress. Caseworkers follow a structured process that includes assessment, planning, referral, and follow-up, ensuring that interventions are tailored to each person’s needs and circumstances. Child protection case management focuses on engaging children and their caregivers in decisions that prioritize the child’s best interests, while GBV case management applies a survivor-centred approach that respects the survivor’s rights, choices, and dignity. MHPSS case management is embedded across health and protection sectors, offering multi-layered support that ranges from community-based psychosocial care to referrals for specialized mental health services. Together, these services promote safety, recovery, and resilience through coordinated, holistic support.

Awareness-raising

Awareness-raising is a key strategy in UNHCR’s protection programming, aimed at increasing knowledge, shifting harmful norms, and empowering communities to recognize and respond to protection risks. Child protection awareness sessions focus on children’s rights, the impact of violence and neglect, and the importance of education and positive parenting. GBV awareness activities promote gender equality, challenge discriminatory practices, and inform communities about available services and legal protection. MHPSS awareness efforts address stigma around mental health, promote emotional well-being, and provide practical guidance on managing stress, trauma, and other psychosocial challenges. These sessions are delivered in safe, accessible spaces and are designed to foster inclusive dialogue and community engagement.

Explosive Ordnance Risk Education

UNHCR, through its 12 partners, conducted explosive ordnance risk education (EORE) awareness sessions across 52 community centres in 14 governorates. These sessions aimed to sensitize communities to the dangers of unexploded ordnance, emphasizing three key safety messages: “Don’t Touch – Move Away – Report.”

Participants received illustrated brochures with key messages provided by the United Nations Mine Action Service (UNMAS), ensuring that these life-saving messages remain accessible after the sessions. The initiative reinforces the importance of avoiding hazardous items and reporting them promptly to prevent injuries and save lives.

Community engagement

UNHCR supports community-based structures that strengthen local capacity to protect and support vulnerable individuals. In child protection, structures such as children’s clubs and child welfare committees empower children and community members to identify risks, advocate for rights, and support peers. GBV programming engages women and men through dedicated committees that promote gender equality, raise awareness, and support survivors in accessing services and opportunities. MHPSS community engagement includes inclusive care programmes for older persons and persons with disabilities, as well as recreational and peer support activities that foster social cohesion and emotional resilience. These initiatives build trust, promote ownership, and ensure that protection responses are rooted in the lived realities of the communities they serve.

related.title: Poland could cut arms aid to Ukraine as WWII spat continues
related.summary: Defense Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz published previously secret data on the scale of Poland's military aid since the outbreak of the war. Relations between Poland and Ukraine have been mired in crisis since Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy gave a military unit the honorary title "Heroes of the UPA." The initials stand for the Ukrainian Insurgent Army, which was instrumental to the killing of up to 100,000 Polish civilians during World War II.
bullets: Defense Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz published previously secret data on the scale of Poland's military aid since the outbreak of the war.

Relations between Poland and Ukraine have been mired in crisis since Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy gave a military unit the honorary title "Heroes of the UPA." The initials stand for the Ukrainian Insurgent Army, which was instrumental to the killing of up to 100,000 Polish civilians during World War II.
The opposition accuses pro-EU Prime Minister Donald Tusk of putting Poland's own military defense at risk.

Polish President Nawrocki says glorifying the UPA is "nonnegotiable" Image: Yauhen Yerchak/SOPA Images/Sipa USA/picture alliance Polish President Karol Nawrocki and Zelenskyy sought a way out of the crisis on the sidelines of the NATO summit in Ankara on Wednesday — without success.
The National Movement has long demanded an end to military aid for Ukraine.
related.excerpt: Relations between Poland and Ukraine have been mired in crisis since Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy gave a military unit the honorary title "Heroes of the UPA." The initials stand for the Ukrainian Insurgent Army, which was instrumental to the killing of up to 100,000 Polish civilians during World War II. Poland is marking a national day of remembrance for the victims on Saturday. Since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022, Poland has provided Ukraine with extensive military support, including weapons and equipment. Until recently, military cooperation between the neighboring countries, which both view Russia as an existential threat, had been accepted by all political parties and was largely kept separate from Poland's domestic political disputes. Lingering 'historical issues' Poland's far-right opposition is attacking the center-right government over the delivery of Patriot interceptor missiles to Ukraine. bullets: LATIN AMERICA & THE CARIBBEAN Weekly Situation Update As of 10 July 2026 The boundaries and names shown and the designations used on this map do not imply official endorsement or acceptance by the United Nations.

Following visits to affected communities and meetings with national and international humanitarian partners, UN Under- Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs and Emergency Relief Coordinator Tom Fletcher announced an appeal for an additional US$298 million to meet the needs of 1.3 million people over the next six months.

The population requiring humanitarian food assistance across the country is expected to rise gradually to between 4.0 and 4.99 million people, with poor rural, Indigenous, Afro-Colombian, Venezuelan migrant, and informal urban households identified as populations of highest concern.
In Kenscoff, attacks beginning the night of 4-5 July and spreading on 8 July displaced 5,840 people (1,836 households).
According to FEWS NET’s latest outlook, crisis (IPC Phase 3) levels of food insecurity are expected to persist through January 2027 in the departments of La Guajira and Chocó.
